label: first copied token m fed back (step L+1 input = m)
explanation: Fires at the first copy-phase step after <DEL> (t = L+1, outputting original token 1) when the fed-back input is m, i.e. sequences that start with m. Holds ~98% of activation mass with ~99% precision. Magnitude is high (~0.6-1.0 of max) for L >= 4, increasing with L / to_go; with L=3 it is mostly silent (the false positives). Missed activations are weak (<0.1 of max): m input at later copy steps (e.g. second m in sequences beginning m m, ~0.15), and faint firing at recall_idx 1 for other first tokens (x, r, o). Does not fire in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on m inputs at other copy positions beyond trace levels.

issues: Minor overclaim: 'does not fire in the original phase' is not strictly true. There are 71 dev activations at orig_idx 6-8, but they carry 0.000 of the mass (trace level).

The ~0.15 figure for the second m in 'm m...' sequences is not well supported. Shown examples are around 0.02 (e.g. 'm m l l m o 0 l' gives 0.02). recall_idx==2 & m has 0.11 precision and 0.7% of mass, so this firing is trace level. It does not change the verdict.

The ~5281 test misses (24% of active steps by count, 1.7% of mass) are scattered weak firing. They fall at recall_idx 1 with other inputs (precision 0.007, 0.9% of mass) and at recall_idx 2 with m (0.7% of mass). No systematic class with real magnitude remains: the coverage of activation quartiles 2 to 4 is 0.99 to 1.0.
The L=3 false positives are confirmed. Adding L > 3 gives test precision 1.000 and F1 0.855, against 0.859 for the base predicate. Strictly, the label should mention L >= 4.
